newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Energy, bank shares down on Swiss reorganisation.
newsitem.headline: Energy, bank shares down on Swiss reorganisation.

text.p: Shares in Swiss power utilities and two big banks lost ground on Monday despite a slightly firmer overall market, after weekend announcements of reorganisation in the Swiss energy sector.
Elektrowatt AG lost 17 Swiss francs or 3.75 percent by mid-day after announcing it was spinning off its utility business as a separate group to be named Watt AG.
Motor-Columbus was down 170 Swiss francs or six percent at 2560 after its biggest shareholder, Union Bank of Switzerland, said it was selling a 40 percent stake and retaining 35.6 percent.
Bank group CS Holding, which has 44.9 percent of Elektrowatt, slipped 1.50 or just over one percent to 137.25 Swiss francs.
Traders said CS was pressured by disappointment that it had not announced a sale of its stake in Elektrowatt, which the bank group wants to get rid of but has set no deadline for selling.
Motor-Columbus was down because of a lower share price of 2,600 Swiss francs that was the basis of the share package sale by UBS. M-C had closed on Friday at 2,730.
UBS bearer shares were down by 10 Swiss francs or 0.8 percent at 1,218.

Like CS Holding, UBS has said it wants to get out of all non-core holdings including Motor-Columbus. Traders said markets were slightly disappointed that UBS plans to retain its remaining 35.6 percent in M-C for the time being.
Utility KW Laufenburg, which belongs to Elektrowatt, fell 16 Swiss francs to 265.
Motor-Columbus's main asset, utility Atel, lost 13 Swiss francs to 870.
